Hi Sergio —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement has asked us to formalize payment terms for our pilot before we sign. Two asks from our side: 1) Can Redwood grant a temporary net60 for Aurora’s first three invoices to align with our internal payment cycle, and 2) can we increase the immediate credit cap to $125k for the pilot period?

Operationally we’d like a "swingline" option so Aurora can sweep 50% of a balance earlier if approval lands in our cycle — essentially a partial early remittance triggered by PO release. We understand this is non-standard; if there’s a short commercial guardrail or deposit you prefer, happy to discuss.

Please confirm the invoicing entity Redwood will use and whether Redwood can include VAT registration details on the invoice.

Hi Leah — thanks for the PO and clear ask. We can support a short-term arrangement while we run the pilot, but we need to align on commercial guardrails and credit checks before committing to a $125k cap.

Proposal from our side to move quickly:
- Temporary payment rhythm: start with net45 for the first two invoices (to reduce early cash exposure) and move to net60 after two consecutive on-time payments.
- Swingline: we can enable a single partial early-sweep (up to 50% of invoice) subject to an approved PO + confirmation email from Aurora finance. This would be a one-time trigger per invoice month for the pilot.
- Credit cap: provisional increase to $100k immediately; full $125k after completed credit references and signed credit application.

Also, can you confirm the VAT billing entity (Aurora Health Europe B.V. or a different subsidiary) and supply the VAT number and billing address? Kar thik (legal) and Marissa (finance) are on Cc to finish the paperwork and set up the DocuSign SOW.

I’ve asked Marissa to share the credit checklist and a draft of the short-term commercial term we’d use for the pilot.

Best,
Sergio
